q: The first non-passenger train in pre-independent India was made operational in:
e: The correct answer is 1851. the first non-passenger (goods) train in pre-independent India ran in 1851, hauling construction material for the Solani Aqueduct near Roorkee. This was two years before the first passenger train of 1853. Related exam fact: India's first passenger train ran on 16 April 1853 between Bori Bunder (Mumbai) and Thane, covering 34 km. This provision exists for a practical reason in day-to-day railway working; keeping that practical picture in mind makes the fact far easier to retain than memorising it in isolation.

q: The GIP Railway Company (GIP) was incorporated in England by an Act of the British Parliament on:
e: 1st August 1849 — that is the right answer. the Great Indian Peninsula (GIP) Railway Company was incorporated in England by an Act of the British Parliament on this date. It went on to build India's first passenger railway line (Mumbai–Thane, 1853). Related exam fact: Lord Dalhousie, as Governor-General, strongly promoted railway construction through his famous Railway Minute of 1853. This provision exists for a practical reason in day-to-day railway working; keeping that practical picture in mind makes the fact far easier to retain than memorising it in isolation.

q: The formation of the Railway Board in 1905 was based upon the recommendations of:

q: The concept which requires that the same accounting method should be used from one accounting period to the next is called

e: The correct answer is Business Entity. Business Entity is a basic accounting CONCEPT, not one of the three fundamental accounting assumptions. q: Mr. Raj purchased goods costing 1,50,000 and sold 4/5th of the goods amounting to Rs.1,80,000. He met expenses amounting to Rs.25,000 during the year, 2018. He made a net profit as Rs.35,000. Which of the accounting concept was followed by him?

q: What is the Accounting Standard for Depreciation?

q: ‘For each and Every Debit there must be a corresponding Credit’ is the principal of____

q: A trial balance will not balance if

e: The correct answer is Profit & Loss account. indirect expenses (office, selling, administration) are transferred to the Profit & Loss Account, while direct expenses go to the Trading Account.
